question: We have two tests to diagnose a serious prognosis disease. Test A has a sensitivity of 95% and a specificity of 60% and test B has a sensitivity of 70% and a specificity of 99%. We have an effective treatment but that produces important adverse effects and also has a very high cost. What test would we choose to make the diagnosis?

options.opa: Test A because it will detect less false positives.
options.opb: Test A because it has a higher sensitivity.
options.opc: Test B because it will detect more false positives.
options.opd: Test A because it will detect more false negatives.
options.ope: Test B because it has a greater specificity.

analysis: In this scenario, the choice of test depends on the balance between sensitivity and specificity, considering the implications of false positives and false negatives. Test A has a higher sensitivity, meaning it is better at detecting true positives, but its lower specificity means it will produce more false positives. Given the high cost and adverse effects of the treatment, minimizing false positives is crucial to avoid unnecessary treatment. Test B, with its higher specificity, will produce fewer false positives, making it a more suitable choice despite its lower sensitivity. Therefore, Test B is preferred to ensure that only those who truly have the disease are treated.
